newsitem.title: USA: Florida tobacco trial interrupted by juror illness.
newsitem.headline: Florida tobacco trial interrupted by juror illness.

text.p: Testimony was suspended on Friday in the wrongful death case against R.J. Reynolds Tobacco Co after a juror fell sick, a court official said.
"A juror was sick and court was suspended until 1:30 p.m.," the court official said.

When court was suspended, Dr. Allan Feingold, a pulmonary specialist, was testifying on behalf of the family of Jean Connor, a 49-year-old woman and long-time smoker who died of lung cancer two years ago.
The judge in the case against R.J. Reynolds, a unit of RJR Nabisco Holdings Corp, is expected to decide later on Friday whether the sick juror can continue or will be replaced by an alternate.
